reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified. The spec (SG-002, line 14-16 in fulu-p2p-interface/SG-002_verify_data_column_sidecar.mmd) explicitly requires checking len(kzg_commitments) <= max_blobs_per_block(epoch), with rejection on violation. The implementation at data_column_verification.rs:532-561 omits this check entirely—only verifying empty check and length consistency, not the epoch-specific upper bound. Block verification does enforce this check (block_verification.rs:883-886). Attack path verified: SSZ VariableList accepts up to MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock=4096 (eth_spec.rs:436), while epoch-specific limits are typically 6-9 blobs. An attacker can craft a data column sidecar with excessive commitments (e.g., 100 when epoch limit is 6), causing resource exhaustion during KZG batch verification (kzg_utils.rs:49-89 processes all cells/proofs). This is a P2P gossip attack requiring only a single network packet, affecting Lighthouse nodes running Fusaka. Severity calibrated: Single-client bug (Lighthouse only, estimated <33% network share). Per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE severity definitions, Medium severity applies to attacks bringing down >5% of the network via single packet. Lighthouse represents significant but not dominant share—estimated 15-25% of CL nodes. This qualifies as Medium severity.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Fulu P2P Interface spec SG-002 (verify_data_column_sidecar) lines 13-16: epoch-specific max_blobs_per_block check is mandatory, with explicit rejection path q_reject_limit.
